materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure outlined a specific 'AI strategy' with three distinct priorities (portfolio, partnerships, open software). The 2025 disclosure replaces this structured strategic framework with a broader, more aspirational positioning as an 'end-to-end AI leader' spanning cloud, edge, and endpoint. This shifts the disclosure from specific operational priorities to a high-level market positioning statement, representing a change in how the company articulates its strategic direction.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Shift from specific AI priorities to broad positioning

comparisons.peer_summary: The company's strategy focuses on technology leadership in semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, achieved through strategic acquisitions and internal R&D to maintain market leadership and drive diversified financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom (AVGO) emphasize technology leadership and strategic partnerships/acquisitions to maintain their competitive position. AMD's strategy involves 'expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships we have established across the ecosystem to accelerate deployments.' Broadcom's strategy focuses on 'technology leadership... achieved through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development.' Both companies rely on a combination of internal R&D and external ecosystem engagement (partnerships for AMD, acquisitions for Broadcom) to deliver their infrastructure technology products.

Our strategy is focused on technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions delivering a comprehensive suite of innovative infrastructure technology products to the world's leading business and government customers.

We seek to achieve this through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development, to ensure our products retain their technology market leadership.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's strategy to win is focused on four key themes: product competitiveness, open platforms, manufacturing at scale, and its people, leveraging its strengths in silicon, platforms, software, and packaging.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel define their core strategic priorities using a enumerated list of key themes. AMD focuses on three priorities: delivering hardware/software portfolios, expanding ecosystem partnerships, and providing open software experiences. Intel focuses on four key themes: product competitiveness, open platforms, manufacturing at scale, and people. Both disclosures emphasize 'open' approaches (AMD's 'open ROCm software platform' and Intel's 'open platforms') and ecosystem/deployment acceleration as central to their AI and computing strategies.

sentences.text: Our AI strategy is focused on three priorities.
The second is expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships we have established across the ecosystem to accelerate deployments of AMD based AI solutions at scale.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

With these strengths and the tailwinds of the superpowers driving digital disruption, our strategy to win is focused on four key themes: product competitiveness, open platforms, manufacturing at scale, and our people.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron is an industry leader in innovative memory and storage solutions, delivering high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR products through Micron® and Crucial® brands to enable advances in AI and compute-intensive applications.
comparisons.comparison: While AMD's strategy focuses on general-purpose adaptive hardware and software for AI, Micron's strategy centers on memory and storage solutions as the enabling infrastructure for AI advancements. AMD highlights 'delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware' for AI, whereas Micron states its 'innovations... fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications.' Both disclose their strategic focus on supporting the AI data economy, with AMD providing the compute/platform layer and Micron providing the critical memory/storage layer.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA extends its AI leadership by providing a complete end-to-end accelerated computing platform for training and inferencing, including GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, DGX Cloud, and NeMo, supported by a large ecosystem of developers and partners.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA articulate their strategy around providing a 'complete, end-to-end' platform that integrates hardware and software to drive AI leadership. AMD's strategy includes 'delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions' and extending an 'open and proven software platform.' Similarly, NVIDIA provides a 'complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI' that includes GPUs, CPUs, DPUs, and software solutions like NeMo, reinforcing its position through a 'large and expanding ecosystem.' Both companies view the integration of full-stack solutions and ecosystem expansion as critical to their competitive strategy.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose strategic investments in hardware architecture and AI-specific engines to support their broader computing strategies. AMD focuses on 'high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions' and an 'open... software platform.' Qualcomm details its 'System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features' including specialized engines like the 'Qualcomm AI Engine' and 'Hexagon NPU' for on-device AI. Both companies leverage dedicated hardware accelerators and software stacks to enable AI capabilities, though AMD targets data center/cloud scale while Qualcomm targets on-device/mobile endpoints.

sentences.text: The first is delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.

Our Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU is a key processor in our AI Engine and is designed for sustained, high-performance AI inference, enabling leading on-device AI capabilities with very low power consumption.
